deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. Folio 61v is a printed page, numbered 10, of a Berlin University lecture catalogue, the German 'Verzeichniss der Vorlesungen'. Nothing on it is in Riemann's hand: there are no marginalia, calculations or annotations.

The page continues the section 'Kunstlehre und Kunstgeschichte' from the previous page. It lists:
- Waagen (referred to as 'derselbe') on the history of architecture, sculpture and painting from 1789 to the present.
- A. B. Marx on choral singing exercises and on composition, Part II of his Lehrbuch, 2nd edition.

It then opens the section 'Philologische Wissenschaften und Erklärung von Schriftstellern', with courses by:
- Böckh (encyclopaedia and methodology of philology; Pindar).
- Bopp (Sanskrit; Mahâbhârata).
- A. Benary (Sanskrit, Latin, Greek; Tacitus).
- G. Curtius (comparative Greek and Latin; Latin grammar).
- Gerhard (Greek mythology).
- Lauer (Odyssey books ε–μ).
- Geppert (Aristophanes' Clouds; Plautus' Mostellaria).
- Heyse (Plato's Cratylus).
- Franz (Aristotle's Politics; disputation exercises; Greek).
- Märcker (Aristotle's Metaphysics).
- Bekker (Aeschines against Ctesiphon).
- Lachmann (Horace's Epistles; Nibelungen).
- Toelken (Ars poetica).
- Zumpt (Quintilian Book X).
- J. Grimm (German grammar).
- v. d. Hagen (Notker's Boethius; Nibelungenlied, 4th edition 1842).
- Uhlemann (Hebrew and Syriac).
- The entry for Petermann (Chaldaic, Syriac, Samaritan) begins here and continues overleaf.

Internal evidence dates the catalogue to Berlin, about 1846–1848:
- the 1842 Nibelungen edition;
- G. Curtius as Privatdozent in Berlin (1845–49);
- Wetzstein and Dieterici, named on the neighbouring pages.

This matches Riemann's Berlin study period (1847–49). The catalogue was presumably kept among his papers as a record of the semester in which he chose courses, for example with Dirichlet, Jacobi, Steiner and Eisenstein. Its value is purely biographical and contextual. No derivation exists to reconstruct.

results.what: Printed Berlin University lecture catalogue page (philology and fine-arts courses), c. 1846–1848, preserved in Riemann's Nachlass

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains no mathematics and no handwriting by Riemann. It is a printed course catalogue, plausibly from his Berlin student years. It is only marginally of biographical interest.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription is essentially faithful to the printed text.

Several passages are partly obscured or overprinted in the image, so their readings are reconstructions from the surrounding text: the line after 'Mahâ-Bhârata erklärt derselbe' ('Mittwochs und Sonnabends von 5-6 Uhr'), 'Dienstags und Mittwochs von 1-2 Uhr privatim' in the Quintilian entry, and 'Hr. Dr. J. Grimm' (printed as 'Grim~').
Greek in the Odyssey entry is printed as '(ε—μ)'.
The spelling 'Toelken' on this page differs from 'Tölken' on the previous page; the print itself has this variation.
